definitions.explanation: The electrical cable that connects an appliance or device to a power outlet. An everyday item found on most electronic devices.

examples.japanese: {電源|でんげん}コードを{抜|ぬ}いてください。
{電源|でんげん}コードが{短|みじか}くて{届|とど}かない。
examples.english: The power cord is too short and doesn't reach.

examples.japanese: {掃除機|そうじき}の{電源|でんげん}コードが{絡|から}まってしまったので、ほどくのに{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: The vacuum cleaner's power cord got tangled, so it took a while to untangle it.

notes:
A compound of {電源|でんげん} (power source) and コード (cord, from English). This is the standard term for the cable that connects an electrical appliance to a wall outlet.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {電源|でんげん}コードを{挿|さ}す: to plug in the power cord
- {電源|でんげん}コードを{抜|ぬ}く: to unplug the power cord
- {電源|でんげん}コードが{断線|だんせん}する: the power cord breaks/frays
- {電源|でんげん}コードを{巻|ま}く: to wind up the power cord

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {電源|でんげん}ケーブル: power cable — essentially the same; ケーブル is often used for thicker or more technical cables
- {延長|えんちょう}コード: extension cord — an additional cord to extend reach
- {充電|じゅうでん}ケーブル: charging cable — specifically for charging devices (USB, etc.)
- コンセント: electrical outlet, power socket — the wall receptacle itself (Japanese English from 'concentric plug')

USAGE:
In product manuals and safety labels, you will often see warnings like {電源|でんげん}コードを{無理|むり}に{曲|ま}げないでください (Do not forcefully bend the power cord).
